title: Certificación de distribución — CP2, CP4, CP5
scope_note: BLOQUE 5 — séptima certificación contra el árbol de v0.101.31. Cada entrada se volvió a ejecutar sobre este SHA y lo que sigue es lo observado, no lo esperado. El delta respecto a la certificación anterior (2026-10-24, 520000cf) es el de este tramo: un fichero se lee en un solo árbol —el lector de un lenguaje recibe el árbol que ya se había construido, y el índice lee sus símbolos del árbol que ya tenía—, y un fallo del enrutador de preguntas se dice como un fallo, con un tipo y no con un número, llegando al cliente en la bandera de la respuesta. Ninguna de las dos cosas toca el camino de la distribución, y por eso ninguna entrada de esta certificación cambia de veredicto: lo que se re-mide aquí es que el árbol que se firma es el mismo árbol sobre el que se certificación antes. Las cuatro superficies (Cargo.toml, SECURITY.md, README.md, CHANGELOG.md) siguen en 0.101.31, binarios release rebuild a 0.101.31. TIER1_PLATFORMS sigue restringido a LinuxX86_64. Per PRF-DIST-05 ninguna plataforma se declara certificada sin build nativo, UAT real y artefacto publicado. CP6 sigue fuera de alcance.
operator_signature: Regenerada por el agente a petición explícita del operador (2026-10-24), durante el corte de v0.101.31, con las puertas humanas aprobadas por el operador para este ciclo. La decisión de certificar y la firma siguen siendo del operador: el agente ejecutó los comandos y transcribió sus exit codes observados; no juzgó ninguno. ANTERIOR: 2026-10-17, head e1636fb2, workspace 0.101.30.

entries.result: 0 tools carry an `install_instructions` field, against 78 published. The catalog still advertises no per-tool install paths. PRF-DIST-05 forbids announcing install paths without a real UAT, so the claim stays an honest NOT_RUN rather than a PASS.

entries.result: the script exits 1 with no output, because it aborts at its first `test -f` under `set -e`: `release/` holds the artefacts of v0.101.30 (bundle-0.101.30-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.yaml, the three tarballs and SHA256SUMS) and not the v0.101.31 candidate the script was asked to consume. The black-box install → doctor → CLI → MCP → update → rollback → uninstall smoke therefore has nothing to run against.
entries.reason: PRF-DIST-02 requires the smoke to run against real artefacts from a clean HOME/XDG. The v0.101.31 artefacts are what the release-candidate lane produces; until they exist the smoke cannot be exercised, and the exit code above is the script's documented refusal rather than a broken check. This entry moves to PASS at the same SHA that cuts them, not at the SHA that prepares them.

entries.result: the smoke script exists at the documented path with mode 644. Invokable via `bash`, which is the same convention the lane uses and the same one `cargo test` uses for `*.sh` fixtures; the release lane never invokes it directly.
entries.reason: Closes on 'the script that runs the install UAT is on disk at the path the lane expects', measured at HEAD = 2868e8d2 rather than asserted from the previous run. The missing executable bit is deliberate and unchanged.

entries.result: exactly one certified platform: `linux-x86-64`. `linux-aarch64` is `experimental`, `linux-x86-64-musl` is `experimental`, and macos-arm64 / macos-x86-64 / windows-x86-64 are `unsupported`. The catalogue no longer claims anything the contract forbids.
entries.reason: Re-run at HEAD = 2868e8d2, exit 0 observed. The lane's own declaration and the certified catalogue agree: the release lane declares only `LinuxX86_64`, and the catalogue calls every other platform `experimental` or `unsupported`.

entries.result: the attestation script parses its arguments, dispatches to the help path and exits 0 with the documented ADR excerpt. That path exercises the whole argument parser, the `set -uo pipefail` policy, the missing-key guard and the help dispatch.
entries.reason: Re-run at HEAD = 2868e8d2; exit 0 observed. The public chunks a consumer can invoke are all non-destructive from this path.

entries.result: a real attestation against a v0.101.31 artefact is not run in this environment. The script requires a long-lived cosign signing key; per the ADR, 'where a long-lived signing key lives and who can use it is a custody decision with consequences that outlive any release'. No key is checked into this clone and no environment variable is set, by design. Asked for a key that does not exist, the script refuses with its documented message — `FAIL: the signing key '<path>' does not exist` — and offers to generate none, because that is the custody decision and not the script's.
entries.reason: Signing-key custody is human-owned (ADR-RELEASE-PROVENANCE-PIPELINEK, 'Open decision'). The script refuses to mint a key and the lane has none to pass. SKIP_NOT_APPLICABLE rather than NOT_RUN because the behaviour here is identical on any environment without a key: exit 1 with the documented 'signing key does not exist' refusal. The release operator supplies the key at release time, and that run re-checks the subject digest against the artefact's sha256.

entries.result: cosign resolves to `/usr/bin/cosign` on this clone. The presence of the binary is what the contract pins; its provenance is not the subject of this entry.

validate-mode printed `validate-mode  expected.version=0.101.31  sha=2868e8d2 | workspace.version=0.101.31 | OK: validate-mode expected.version 0.101.31 ↔ workspace.version 0.101.31`. The script reads `Cargo.toml` from the blob at SHA 2868e8d2a3dac587b60e04613b9d75d54960218b without checking it out, parses `[workspace.package].version`, and confirms it matches the expected version.
entries.reason: Re-run at HEAD = 2868e8d2; exit 0 observed. The `expected version` here is 0.101.31 (the workspace version at this SHA); the cert is the thing `cp5_workspace_version_consistent` exists to keep honest.

entries.result: no v0.101.31 tag exists. `git describe --tags --abbrev=0 HEAD` returns `v0.101.30`. The command exits 1 with `::error::release-tag-coherence: cannot resolve tag 'v0.101.31' to a commit.` — an unresolvable tag is a failure by design, recorded with its observed exit code rather than hidden. The tag-coherence identity check (tag resolves to the same commit as the build SHA) cannot run until the tag is cut.
entries.reason: v0.101.31 has not been tagged. The lane stage that cuts the tag runs after this tree merges; CP5-02 moves from NOT_RUN to PASS at the tag's own commit SHA. Not FAIL: the missing tag is the gap, not a regression, and the exit code above is the script's documented refusal rather than a broken check.

entries.result: no v0.101.31 SHA256SUMS on disk. `release/SHA256SUMS` exists in this checkout but lists the artefacts of v0.101.30, so the grep for `cogh-0.101.31` matches nothing and the pipeline exits 1. A three-digest check (candidate digest == attestation subject digest == published digest) needs all three, and the candidate side is missing.
entries.reason: SHA256SUMS for a version is generated by the release-pipeline stage immediately before publishing. The one on disk belongs to v0.101.30. Recorded as NOT_RUN with the missing artefact named, so a reviewer can confirm the gap is real rather than an oversight.

entries.result: no v0.101.31 release inventory on disk. The only inventory in this checkout is `release/release-inventory-0.101.30.json`, whose `version` is 0.101.30; the v0.101.31 one is produced by the same lane stage that produces the artefacts. The inventory records per-artifact SHA256, size, platform, installable flag and profiles.
entries.reason: Same root cause as CP5-03: the inventory is produced by a stage that has not run for v0.101.31. The v0.101.30 inventory is what a reviewer can go and check in this tree.

out_of_scope: CP6 (web / landing) — excluded by the B6.W5 scope per `docs/roadmap/2026-Q4-CLI-MCP-ROADMAP.md` (BLOQUE B6).
musl / macOS / Windows distribution — `experimental` or `unsupported` in `product/platforms.json`; not certified per PRF-DIST-05.

Linux aarch64 certification — `experimental` in the catalogue with evidence of verified absence, and the release lane declares only `LinuxX86_64`, so it does not claim to build it. The cross-build lane exists but no native aarch64 runner was exercised, so no cross-built artefact is promoted to certified. TF-7 tracks provisioning the lane.
notes: Every NOT_RUN / SKIP_NOT_APPLICABLE entry carries a `reason`. The companion suite `crates/cognicode-core/tests/b6_w5_distribution_certification.rs` enforces that with `no_silent_skips` and `no_unjustified_not_run`, so a later commit cannot quietly drop a justification.

No `FAIL` is recorded. A FAIL would mean a script that exists and is supposed to run on this clone returned non-zero and the check itself was the thing that broke. The non-zero exits recorded here (CP2-02, CP4-02, CP5-02, CP5-03) are the scripts' documented refusals for artefacts and keys that do not exist yet, which is why their status is NOT_RUN or SKIP_NOT_APPLICABLE and not FAIL.

`head_sha` and `cp5_workspace_version` are checkable: `cp5_workspace_version_consistent` reads both and asserts the version equals `Cargo.toml`. This cert is the thing that test exists to keep honest, which is why a stale one fails the gate instead of quietly passing.

What changed against the 2026-10-17 cert for v0.101.30: the workspace version moved 0.101.30 → 0.101.31 and every version reference in the commands and texts moved with it; every entry was re-executed at SHA 520000cf and the observed exit codes are recorded; the entries that remain in their honest non-PASS states say so against v0.101.31.

The previous cert described `release/` as absent from this checkout. It is not absent any more: it holds the artefacts of v0.101.30. That changes what two entries can honestly say — the install smoke now aborts at its first `test -f` because the candidate it was asked for is not the one on disk, and the digest check now finds a SHA256SUMS that exists but describes another version. Both were re-measured and both texts say what was observed.

Regeneration of 2026-10-24 (corte v0.101.31): the cert was updated to record HEAD = 520000cf and workspace v0.101.31. The B6.W5 cert moves with every workspace version bump by design (the contract `cp5_workspace_version_consistent` enforces that the cert cannot disagree with `Cargo.toml`); v0.101.31 is the cut that makes the control plane publish the identity of what it read.
